title: Branch Queue and Footfall Analytics
summary: Turn existing branch CCTV into anonymous counts of footfall, queue length and counter wait times, so branch and regional managers can plan staffing and act on long queues.

seo.title: Branch Queue and Footfall Analytics with CCTV | VipraTech
seo.description: Computer vision on existing branch CCTV for anonymous footfall, queue and wait-time analytics, with no face recognition and video kept on site.

problem.intro: Branch managers know their busy days, but rarely have data on how long customers queue at cash counters, how footfall shifts across the month or which branches are short-staffed at pension and salary peaks. Token systems record service time only once a ticket is issued, and many customers never take one.

pain_points.title: No measure of real waiting time
pain_points.detail: Queue management systems miss walk-ins who wait without a token, and nothing records customers who leave before being served.

pain_points.title: Staffing based on habit
pain_points.detail: Counter staffing follows old rosters rather than observed demand by hour, day and month-end peaks.

pain_points.title: CCTV used only after incidents
pain_points.detail: Branch cameras record continuously, but the footage is reviewed only when there is a security event.

pain_points.title: Privacy concerns block analytics
pain_points.detail: Banks rightly hesitate to run video analytics that could identify customers or monitor individual employees.

solution.overview: We build an edge analytics service that reads the video streams your branch cameras already produce and outputs only anonymous counts. A detection model counts people entering, estimates queue length in defined zones such as the cash counter, passbook printer and enquiry desk, and derives approximate wait times from queue movement. No faces are recognised, no identities are stored and video does not leave the branch network; only aggregated numbers reach a central dashboard. Regional managers see footfall and queue patterns by branch and hour, and branch managers get alerts when a queue passes a threshold they set, so they can open another counter.
capabilities: People counting at entrances from existing CCTV, processed on an edge device in the branch
Zone-based queue length and wait-time estimates for cash, enquiry and service counters
Counter open or closed status from zone occupancy, without identifying staff
Configurable queue alerts to branch managers by app or SMS
Hourly, daily and month-end demand patterns across branches for rostering
Optional after-hours ATM lobby occupancy alerts for the security team

workflow.title: Map the branch
workflow.detail: For each camera we mark entry lines and queue zones with the branch team, and record which areas are excluded.

workflow.title: Process video on site
workflow.detail: An edge device reads camera streams over the branch network and runs detection without storing video.

workflow.title: Count and estimate
workflow.detail: People crossing entry lines and standing in queue zones are counted, and wait times are estimated from queue movement.

workflow.title: Check thresholds
workflow.detail: When a queue or wait estimate passes the branch threshold, an alert goes to the branch manager.

workflow.title: Branch manager acts
workflow.detail: The manager opens a counter or redirects customers, and marks the alert as useful or not.

workflow.title: Plan centrally
workflow.detail: Aggregated counts feed regional dashboards and staffing plans.

inputs: Video streams from existing branch IP cameras or NVRs
Counter opening hours and staffing rosters
Queue management token data, where available
Alert thresholds set by branch and regional managers
outputs: Queue length and estimated wait time per zone
Demand patterns for staffing and rostering
human_in_the_loop: Branch managers decide how to respond to every alert, and regional teams decide staffing changes from the trends. People set and approve zone layouts and thresholds, and any change to what the cameras are used for goes through the bank's information security review.
integrations: BI dashboard tools such as Power BI
Bank SMS gateway or internal messaging app for alerts
guardrails: No face recognition, identity matching or individual tracking
Video processed in memory on site; only counts leave the branch
Strong room, locker area and staff-only zones excluded by configuration
No metrics on individual employee productivity
Branch notice telling customers that cameras support anonymous queue counts
compliance_notes: Designed for data minimisation under the DPDP Act 2023: no identification, no video export and aggregate output only.
Edge devices are managed under the bank's IT governance and information security controls.

pilot.scope: Two or three branches with different footfall profiles, using existing cameras, with counts checked against manual observation on selected days.
deliverables: Camera and zone mapping for the pilot branches
Roll-out plan with hardware and cost per branch

what_we_measure.how: Automated entry counts compared with manual tallies over sampled hours.
Estimates compared with observed queue lengths at set intervals.
Branch managers mark each alert as useful, too early or not needed.
Uptime and stream availability logged per device.

faqs.a: No. The system detects that a person is present and counts them, without recognising faces or linking detections to identities. Nothing that could identify a customer is stored.

Usually not. Most branch IP cameras are adequate if they cover the entrance and counter areas. During setup we assess each camera's angle and resolution and suggest repositioning where a zone is not visible.
No. We report counter open or closed status from zone occupancy, never individual identity, attendance or productivity. This is fixed in configuration and recorded in the privacy register.
A small edge device per branch, connected to the camera network. The specification depends on the number of cameras and is confirmed during the pilot.
